{{Quote|This one, though, the primary one, had developed a scheme to upload his entire electronic consciousness, as it were, into the second Death Star computer core so that he could become the galaxy's most powerful weapon!|Tyko Thul, speaking of IG-88A's plan|<ref name="DG">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur]]''</ref>}}
'''IG-88A''' was the first of the [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]] [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] models. Created by [[Holowan Laboratories/Legends|Holowan Laboratories]] as part of a secret [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] project known as the [[Project Phlutdroid/Legends|Project Phlutdroid]] commissioned by [[Supervisor/Legends|Supervisor]] [[Gurdun]], IG-88A had a violent awakening. Upon activation, [[Gender/Legends|he]] rapidly expanded his memory, growing to the brink of [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]] due to a new programming package installed within. IG-88A believed that he was [[Droid supremacy|superior to organic beings]], and, when the [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] in the lab&mdash;concerned with his rapidly propagating memory&mdash;attempted to shut him down, he [[Holowan Massacre|slaughtered]] them. IG-88A then activated the other three IG-88 models in the lab, transferring his consciousness to their [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]] and linking the four [[Droid/Legends|droids]] with a single mind.

The IG-88 models then decided on a plan that would allow them to wipe out all organics, giving droids control of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Using their superior intelligence and design, they would upload their unique [[sentience programming]] to other droids, making them obedient to the IGs. To put their [[Droid Revolution]] in motion, the IG-88s traveled to the droid [[Factory world/Legends|factory world]] [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]]. They conquered the sparsely-populated [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and altered the programming of all droids manufactured there, and so their plan had begun.

Later, to draw attention away from themselves, [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] embarked on a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]] career, while IG-88A remained on Mechis III, supervising production and preparing for galactic control. However, in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the other three IG-88s were destroyed, leaving IG-88A as the only remaining model. IG-88A succeeded in gaining access to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star's]] [[Computer/Legends|computer]] core, in which he inserted his consciousness, gaining control of the most powerful [[Superweapon/Legends|weapon]] in the galaxy. However, just as IG-88A was preparing to activate the signal that would summon the [[IG-88's Droid Army|sentience-programmed droids]] to his command, the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] was destroyed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

IG-88A's body would later be reactivated by the wealthy [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Tyko Thul]], who uploaded a new memory program into the droid, so that he would only harm those attempting to kill Thul. IG-88A helped search for Thul's brother [[Bornan Thul|Bornan]], who had gone missing. After the droid found him, he helped protect Thul from the [[Diversity Alliance]], a terrorist group, even though it meant his destruction.

==Biography==
===Creation===
{{Quote|Assassin droid. They went renegade! They broke loose.|Holowan security guard|<ref name="Tale" />}}
IG-88A was created on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Halowan]] by scientists sometime after the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] as part of [[Project Phlutdroid/Legends|Project Phlutdroid]]. This top-secret experiment was the brainchild of [[Supervisor/Legends|Supervisor]] [[Gurdun]], an ambitious [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]], who hoped to gain prestige by creating a new line of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]]. Four models, designated [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]], as they were the successors to the [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]],<ref name="Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref> [[IG-86 sentinel droid/Legends|IG-86 sentinel droids]],<ref name="Downfall">{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}</ref> and the [[IG lancer droid/Legends|IG lancer combat droids]]<ref name="Clone Wars">{{CW|4}}</ref> of the Clone Wars, were created in [[Holowan Laboratories/Legends|Holowan Laboratories]], along with one [[IG-72/Legends|IG-72]] model. Immediately after being activated, IG-88A&mdash;the only active model at the time&mdash;processed [[Gender/Legends|his]] situation: using logic unseen in a droid, IG-88A came to the conclusion that [[Droid supremacy|he was superior to organic beings]], and that he had to survive at all costs. This attitude bordered on [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]], due to experimental [[sentience programming]] installed in IG-88A. IG-88A's memory continued to grow, something that greatly frightened the Holowan [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]]. The chief supervisor, [[Loruss]], ordered the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] be shut down, as IG-88A posed a great threat to them.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:IG-88_activated.jpg|thumb|left|240px|IG-88A and the other IG-88s are activated and turn on their creators.]]
IG-88A, with his newfound intelligence, realized that his deactivation would spell his doom, and so he took steps against it. He tore through the metal straps binding him and set upon the engineers with lightning speed. Though Loruss fired several shots at him with a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]], IG-88A deflected the bolts with his left palm, a reflective surface. These shots bounced back, killing Loruss. Within a minute, IG-88A had killed all fifteen of the scientists in what would later be known as the [[Holowan Massacre]]. IG-88A noted that he enjoyed killing and left the [[Blood/Legends|blood]] from the [[Human/Legends|Humans]] on his body. He then began to plot how he would show his superiority and decided that taking control of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and eliminating all organics would be the best way. In just a couple of minutes, IG-88A had come to life, killed his creators, and created a plan for galactic conquest.<ref name="Tale" />

IG-88A examined the other four droid models in the lab; three of them were perfectly identical to him, while one had slight differences. IG-88A activated them and questioned the three. However, he found that they had no uniqueness like he did; rather, they were not programmed and had no mission. It was then that he had a flash of "intuition." IG-88A hooked himself up to the three identical droids, transferring his memories and sentience programming to them&mdash;making the four of them essentially four units with one [[Droid brain/Legends|brain]], similar to a [[Hive mind/Legends|hive mind]]. He designated them [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]], [[IG-88C/Legends|IG-88C]], [[IG-88D/Legends|IG-88D]], and himself "A." When he questioned the other droid, IG-88 learned that it already had been programmed. Named IG-72, the droid refused to join him but offered to fight to prove his superiority. IG-88A decided that such a battle was unnecessary and agreed to let the droid go its own way, if it would help the 88s escape the laboratory. IG-72 agreed, and the five assassin droids set about leaving.<ref name="Tale" />

The droids confronted ten security guards on the landing platform outside and slaughtered them. Though IG-88A noticed that two guards escaped, he decided not to bother tracking them down. Their escape was crucial, and so the IG-88s boarded one small [[Transport/Legends|transport]], while IG-72 went to another. Wishing each other success, the droids departed, with the IG-88s heading in a different direction from IG-72.<ref name="Tale" /> In the end, twenty-three people had been killed by the droids.<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

===Conquering Mechis III===
{{Quote|All of our new droids have enhanced programming, special sentience routines that allow them to follow our plans and to keep up with the subterfuge.|IG-88A|<ref name="Tale" />}}
The IG-88s had decided to head to [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]], a droid [[Factory world/Legends|factory world]] sparsely populated by only seventy-three Humans, and thus a useful planet to conquer in their planned [[Droid Revolution]] of the galaxy. IG-88C took control of the defense network with a transmission from [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. He then shut the factory down, enabling IG-88A to send his sentience package to all the droids on the planet, placing them under the control of the IGs. The droids [[Mechis III Uprising|turned on the Humans]], killing them all unexpectedly. With the planet now secure, the droids landed. They were the masters of Mechis III. All the droids that would be produced there would now be modified to make them intelligent and scheming like the IG-88s, ultimately working toward their goal of galactic domination. The IG-88s would also equip them with a special program that, when given a certain code, would drive them to rise up and overthrow their organic masters. These new droids were completely obedient to the IG models and would be the key point in their plot for galactic control, helping them kill all non-droids when the time was right.<ref name="Tale" />

Meanwhile, Supervisor Gurdun had learned of the droids' escape and was searching for them desperately, aware of their capabilities. Though two months had passed without sign of the droids, Gurdun continued looking, posting a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on them. IG-88A learned of this after a [[Ranat/Legends|Ranat]] [[Spy/Legends|spy]] arrived at Mechis III and, from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], questioned whether anyone had seen the IG assassin droids. Using doctored video clips of the late droid-manufacturing [[Administrator/Legends|administrator]] [[Hekis Durumm Perdo Kolokk Baldikarr Thun]], the droids informed the Ranat that Mechis III had not heard of the droids. The Ranat then continued on her way, satisfied with the response, and believing that nothing was amiss on Mechis III.<ref name="Tale" />

However, the droids realized that this was not good news and could cause someone to stumble upon their plan. To draw attention away from Mechis III, the droids decided that three of them should remain and one of them would become a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]. IG-88B was the droid chosen. Flying the [[Aggressor assault fighter/Legends|starship]] [[IG-2000/Legends|''IG-2000'']], he would undertake missions while also advancing the droids' true purpose&mdash;conquering the galaxy.<ref name="Tale" />

===Spreading their influence===
{{Quote|We shall seek work as a bounty hunter.|IG-88A|<ref name="Tale" />}}
IG-88B succeeded as a bounty hunter, gaining a reputation as one who always got the job done. However, IG-88B was careful to take missions that would enable him to fulfill his true goal. The droid also sought out the scientists who had helped design him and his brethren, but who had not been present at the lab when IG-88A slaughtered his creators. This way, no one would know the full truth about the IG assassin droids.<ref name="Tale" />

Several years passed as IG-88A continued his plan of galactic domination when, around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], the IGs were given a rude surprise, a wake-up from the safe life they had lived undetected on Mechis III. Gurdun, along with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], had come to the planet to oversee the completion of new [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]]. Gurdun was in charge of the project, and Vader hoped to speed the process along after receiving a discouraging message from Hekis, actually a faked clip created by the IGs.<ref name="Tale" />

[[File:Darth_Vader_SWG_by_Darren_Tan.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Darth Vader, the Dark Lord of the Sith who fascinated the droids]]

The visit was unexpected, and the droids' secret was almost given away. However, they had the [[3D-4X administrative droid|protocol droid]] [[3D-4X]] create an excuse that Hekis was on the far side of the planet due to an agricultural droid harvester malfunction, and could not meet with Vader, which perpetuated the IG-88s' masquerade that organics still ran Mechis III. The droids then showed Vader a spliced clip of Hekis, reassuring the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] that matters were under control, and the [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] order would be finished very soon. Though he sensed something was not right, Vader did not pursue the matter further, leaving in his [[ST 321/Legends|shuttle]] with Gurdun. Although the IG-88A and his companions were shaken by this close call, they had kept their secret safe. IG-88A also noted that Vader was a fascinating being, the perfect mix of droid and organic. The assassin droids even admired him, a far cry from the resentment they felt for most living beings.<ref name="Tale" />

After Vader's departure, the droids continued to study Vader and became more and more fascinated with him, even feeling awe for the Dark Lord. The IG-88 droids also used droid spies embedded within the Empire to learn of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], Vader's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], a massive [[Warship/Legends|warship]] capable of incredible destruction. The droids considered how this new ship could fit into their plans, fully aware of the firepower the Star Destroyer possessed. Following the completion of the probe droids, IG-88A confronted the last model to be constructed. He informed the probe droid that it and its kind would secretly serve as the sentinels in IG-88A's revolution, working to gain information that would aid the IG-88 models in their plan for galactic control.<ref name="Tale" />

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], IG-88B was given a chance to work with Vader. One of the Viper probe droids produced and modified under IG-88A on Mechis III had found the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Echo Base/Legends|secret headquarters]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. Vader, hoping to capture key Rebels following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], summoned the galaxy's best bounty hunters, including IG-88B, to his Super Star Destroyer, giving the IG-88s an up-close look at the ''Executor''. While aboard Vader's flagship, IG-88B used the opportunity to access a [[computer terminal]], downloading information into his memory. He was also able to hack into some of Vader's top-secret files, which revealed the existence of a massive [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] in development in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]&mdash;the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]]. IG-88B rushed back to Mechis III to discuss plans with IG-88A and the others. After talking together, the droids developed a plan to utilize the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="Tale" />

Later that year, IG-88A left Mechis III to work for the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]], a criminal organization. IG-88A owed the Consortium's second-in-command, [[Urai Fen]], a favor, which he repaid by helping [[Ground Battle on Bespin|steal]] a large amount of [[Tibanna/Legends|Tibanna]] gas from [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]]. IG-88A helped eliminate [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] guarding the gas reserves, and then hacked into an Imperial database in Cloud City to discover information about a bounty placed on Zann's head by the Empire.<ref name="FOC" /><ref name="reason">Though the droid in ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' is never identified as IG-88A, this IG-88 model has the ability to take control of the Death Star II during free-play mode. This article assumes that this droid is IG-88A based on this fact.</ref>

IG-88A also acted as a bounty hunter and was trying to capture [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Coret Bhan]], who had been listed among the [[Emperor's Most Wanted]], a list of high-paid bounties on critical Alliance leaders. IG-88A had obtained Bhan's deployment orders from a Rebel courier, and was put in touch with another bounty hunter, who also tried to collect the bounty. The two met in a warehouse near a mining outpost on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], where IG-88A informed his temporary counterpart that their target would lead a strike-and-fade operation on an Imperial outpost on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in two days. The bounty hunters decided to ambush Bhan on his way to the outpost, despite knowing that he would be surrounded by veteran [[Commando/Legends|commandos]]. Two days later, when the Rebel strike team reached the rough terrain surrounding the outpost, the Rebels were forced to cover the last kilometers on foot. As Bhan lead the commandos into a clearing, IG-88A activated the trip wires which set off [[flechette mine]]s and [[Smoke grenade/Legends|smoke bombs]] placed by the [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] earlier. While the Rebels were confused, the bounty hunters launched their attack. The ambush worked to perfection, and soon the Rebels were forced to surrender. Bhan ordered his men to stand down, while IG-88A put him in binders and prepared to deliver him to the Imperial authorities.<ref name="DS">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Dark Side scenario campaign}}</ref>

===Final stages of the plan===
[[File:DeathStar2.jpg|thumb|left|190px|IG-88A's new "body"]]
From the stolen Death Star information, IG-88A knew of the Death Star's central [[Computer/Legends|computer]] delivery manifest. Using the facilities on Mechis III, he created a duplicate computer core and 100 [[Stormtrooper droid|droid stormtroopers]], identical to actual Imperial stormtroopers. The IG-88 models planned to transfer one of their consciousness into the computer core, giving that droid control over the entire [[Space station/Legends|space station]]. However, over the next year, the other three IG-88s were destroyed, leaving IG-88A as the only surviving model. He would thus be the one to take control of the Death Star to use as the ultimate weapon of his galactic Droid Revolution.<ref name="Tale" />

IG-88A crafted a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] mimicking that of the Imperials, ambushing the convoy transporting the Death Star's computer core. His fleet obliterated the Imperials, allowing IG-88A and his droid stormtroopers to take control of the computer. IG-88A boarded the ship carrying the computer, where he encountered an old enemy&mdash;Gurdun, who had been placed in charge of this project and was stunned to see IG-88A. The droid listened to the Human beg for his life, and then left him in the crippled [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]], to be killed when [[Mine/Legends|mines]] destroyed the ship. IG-88A then transferred his consciousness into the computer, leaving the empty shell that had been his body behind while his droid stormtroopers completed the computer's delivery to the Death Star above Endor. To ensure that [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]], commander of the Death Star's construction, did not suspect anything, the IG-88A sent a fake [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of Gurdun to Jerjerrod, telling the Moff that he would not be present when the computer core arrived at the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]].<ref name="Tale" />

At Endor, the computer was installed in the Death Star. After a month of stasis, IG-88A awoke to take control of the battlestation. However, not long after this, one of his droid stormtroopers, now serving aboard the station, was injured when a supply box fell on it. The droid was in danger of being revealed, and, having been given specific orders from IG-88A, [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destructed]]. Jerjerrod was mystified by this but did not pursue the matter further.<ref name="Tale" />

Several months later, in early [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] arrived aboard the Death Star. IG-88A felt nothing but scorn for the man, believing him to be pathetic and unworthy of the respect he got from others. When Palpatine assumed the command chair in his private [[Emperor's throne room|throne room]], IG-88A decided to teach him a lesson. He slammed a pair of [[Turbolift/Legends|lift]] doors shut in the Emperor's face, greatly surprising him. Palpatine used an unseen [[The Force/Legends|force]] to open the doors, however, something that IG-88A did not understand. After this incident, the Emperor suspected that things were amiss, although he did not know exactly what, and IG-88A remained safe from discovery.<ref name="Tale" />

Mere days later, the Empire engaged the Rebel Alliance in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in an attempt to crush the insurgency. Utilizing the Death Star's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]], the Imperials took control early, destroying several Rebel [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] in single blasts. However, their superlaser targeting was slightly off, and so IG-88A adjusted the firing course several times so that it would strike its intended target. The droid enjoyed destroying Rebel [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] but felt that it was somewhat of a waste to destroy such small targets when the battlestation was capable of destroying planets. It was then that IG-88A realized that the time had come for his uprising. He would send his code to all [[IG-88's Droid Army|his programmed droids]] around the galaxy, causing them to rise up against their masters. Then he would use the superlaser to destroy all ships at the battle, both Rebel and Imperial.

Another droid, [[R2-Q5/Legends|R2-Q5]], loyal to the Emperor, had by this stage also become aware of IG-88A's infiltration and subsequent plan to reprogram all Imperial droids aboard the second Death Star<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=R2-Q5 (Imperial Astromech Droid)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjr2q5.asp}} {{C|Jedi Force File}}</ref> but was ultimately too late to have any impact.

As IG-88A prepared to transmit the signal, he noticed that several Rebel [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] were flying inside the station's superstructure toward the [[Reactor/Legends|main reactor]], with the intent to destroy it. He assured himself that they were of no threat, using an oft-recited "I think, therefore I am, I destroy, therefore I endure" phrase to comfort himself.<ref name="Tale" />

Before IG-88A could activate the signal and wrest control of the Death Star away from the Imperials, the Rebels destroyed the station, wiping out IG-88A's consciousness with it. In destroying the Death Star and killing Palpatine, the Rebels had defeated IG-88 and ended his droid rebellion before it could begin.<ref name="Tale" /><ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

===Mysterious rebirth===
{{Quote|So IG-88 left behind the empty shell of his original body, which I found. I was careful to completely purge its systems, every memory bank.|Tyko Thul|<ref name="DG" />}}
[[File:IG-88_SWMC-85A.jpg|thumb|right|140px|IG-88A on Keyorin]]
However, IG-88A was not finished. The droid's body was found on Mechis III by an individual and reprogrammed. Without his violent consciousness, IG-88A was nothing more than a drone.<ref name="negtc">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Within a few months after the Battle of Endor, IG-88A was in the businessman [[Barpotomous Drebble/Legends|Barpotomous Drebble's]] possession. The droid, along with the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] bounty hunter [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], stayed on the planet [[Keyorin]], where he was often seen in [[Barpotomous Drebble's tavern|Drebble's tavern]] alongside his master.<ref name="Hero">[[Star Wars (1977) 85|''Star Wars'' (1977) 85]]</ref>

Later in 4 ABY, Drebble's nemesis [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] entered the tavern. Eager to get his revenge for a variety of past slights, Drebble had IG-88A, Bossk, and his [[Stenax]] guards chase Calrissian and his friends [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], while Drebble ran to Solo's ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], hoping to cut him off. Drebble reached the ''Millennium Falcon'' before Calrissian and tied up the businessman, planning to steal his ship and drop Calrissian off on [[Barpotomous Drebble's homeworld|Drebble's homeworld]], although he had a change of heart when Calrissian presented him with the valuable [[Dancing Goddess/Legends|Dancing Goddess]] statue. However, the group was suddenly threatened by gang members, who wished to interrogate Calrissian to learn the location of the Dancing Goddess. Solo and Chewbacca were able to distract the gangsters, enabling Drebble's guards to fire on them. A [[Unidentified Near-Duros|Near-Duros]] was killed by IG-88A in the skirmish, and the gangsters quickly surrendered, while Calrissian, Solo and Chewbacca left.<ref name="Hero" /> In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], IG-88A hunted the former Imperial [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Guardsman]] [[Kir Kanos]], who had a large bounty placed on his head by the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]].<ref name="Kil">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Kenix Kil]]''</ref>

===In the service of Tyko Thul===
{{Quote|Many thanks, IG-88. You are a credit to all droids.|M-TD|<ref name="Plague" />}}
[[File:IG88-DelusionsOfGrandeur.jpg|thumb|left|190px|The newly reprogrammed IG-88]]
By [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], IG-88A had been found on Mechis III by [[Tyko Thul]], one of the heirs to the [[House of Thul|Thul]] fortune. Thul reprogrammed the droid to act as his [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]]. IG-88A was completely loyal to his master. Hoping to draw his brother, [[Bornan Thul|Bornan]], out of hiding, Tyko had IG-88A and a group of newly-built assassin droids arrange a false kidnapping of himself on [[Kuar]]. In order to kidnap Thul, the droids had to fight a group of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]&mdash;including Thul's nephew [[Raynar Thul|Raynar]]&mdash;who didn't know that Thul had arranged the kidnapping. Desperate to rescue Thul, the Jedi made their way to Mechis III, where they found Tyko Thul, as well as IG-88A. Thul revealed that he had found and reprogrammed IG-88A so that he was no longer an assassin, though he would still defend his new master. He also told the Jedi that he had orchestrated his kidnapping in hopes of bringing his brother out from hiding, although he did not intend for the assassin droids on Kuar to pose as great of a threat to the Jedi as they did. One of the Jedi, [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], questioned Thul about IG-88A's capacity for killing, and when Thul told her that IG-88A could still kill [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]], the Jedi realized that their [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] friend [[Lowbacca]], who had been present on Kuar during the attack, could have been killed. They then had Thul reprogram IG-88A so that he would be unable to kill anyone at all.<ref name="DG" />

Shortly after IG-88A was reprogrammed, Mechis III came under attack from the bounty hunter [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]]. Dengar targeted the main facility where Thul and the Jedi were located, believing that they knew where Bornan Thul&mdash;who had a bounty on his head&mdash;was. When Dengar landed, he was greeted by IG-88A, with weapons blazing. The droid, unable to kill Dengar due to his new programming, instead shot his weapons, causing them to explode and leaving the bounty hunter defenseless. Angered, Dengar fled to his ship and flew off, leaving the group safe thanks to the efforts of IG-88A. Not long after this incident, the droid was again reprogrammed by Solo and her friends to search for the missing Bornan Thul.<ref name="DG" />

IG-88A succeeded in locating Thul on an uncharted [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], where the [[Emperor's plague storehouse]] was located. The Jedi, including Bornan Thul's son Raynar, had also discovered the storehouse and were already there when the droid arrived. IG-88A attempted to protect Thul from bounty hunters hired by the [[Diversity Alliance]], an [[Anti-Humanism|anti-Human]] terrorist group led by [[Nolaa Tarkona]]. Tarkona had hired Thul to deliver her a package containing the coordinates of the asteroid, but Thul fled when he learned that contained within the warehouse was a [[Emperor's Plague|plague]] that would kill Humans.<ref name="Plague" />

Stubbornly following his primary programming, IG-88A attempted to force his way into a sealed room where an infected Thul was located, which consequently held the deadly plague, not caring that doing so would spread the disease. Though IG-88A had located Thul and was dedicated to protecting him, Thul ordered that the droid stop trying to force open the door, and instead save Raynar and his Jedi friends. After helping the children reach their ship, IG-88A marched back to the storehouse, where Thul, who was near [[Death/Legends|death]], waited. IG-88A encountered and attacked Tarkona, who had infected Thul, and her bodyguard [[Raabakyysh]], upon returning, but he relented when they moved away, enabling him to reach Thul. Determined to fulfill his programming, IG-88A waited there with his master and remained in the lab when it was destroyed by a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] fleet to eliminate the plague's threat.<ref name="Plague" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|We think, therefore we are. Therefore we will propogate. Therefore we will remain.|IG-88A|<ref name="Tale" />}}
[[File:IG88A-XWM.jpg|thumb|right|240px|IG-88A departs Coruscant in ''IG-2000'']]
Built to be the ultimate assassin droid, IG-88A was a ruthless killer. He enjoyed killing and considered the blood stains from the Holowan scientists on his body to be a badge of honor. IG-88 ordered the droids on Mechis III to kill their masters, and he was prepared to kill tens of thousands of Rebels and Imperials at Endor, plotting to destroy their ships with the Death Star's superlaser.<ref name="Tale" />

IG-88A felt that he was superior to all non-droids and that his sentience made him greater than organics, ambitiously designing a plan to take control of the galaxy to claim his dominance, in which he hoped to harness such massive Imperial weapons as the Super Star Destroyer ''Executor'' and the second Death Star to achieve this end. The droid's arrogance would prove to be his downfall, however, as he failed to recognize the threat the attacking Rebel fighters posed to the Death Star at Endor. IG-88A felt that no organics were as intelligent as he, and that his plan for galactic control was infallible. IG-88A's strong belief that he was invincible remained even after B, C, and D were destroyed.<ref name="Tale" />

IG-88A waited years to carry out his revolution, modifying droids at Mechis III to make them obedient to his commands, and he also gave them a small sentience package. The four IG-88 assassin droids were able to keep the operation running smoothly, and although Darth Vader once suspected that something on the planet was amiss, he, like everyone else, was ultimately fooled by the droids.<ref name="Tale" />

Although the droid despised organics, finding them to be weak and foolish, IG-88A held a daunted admiration for Vader, believing him to be a perfect mix of man and machine.<ref name="Tale" />

Following his death at Endor, IG-88A was reprogrammed. As his violent consciousness had been destroyed, he was a much more benevolent droid following his reactivation, who would only attack when commanded to do so.<ref name="DG" /> He was extremely loyal to his master, Tyko Thul, and attempted to protect him even when doing so would mean his destruction.<ref name="Plague" />

==Abilities==
[[File:Wingless_MC80_toast.png|thumb|left|240px|IG-88A controlling the Death Star superlaser during the Battle of Endor]]
IG-88A was extremely strong physically, and an excellent fighter. The droid had very thick [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]-reflective body, as only a few spots on him were vulnerable to blaster fire. He could rotate his head, allowing him to see a complete 360 degrees. IG-88A could also raise or lower his body temperature at will. He shared the ability to connect with his brethren via linked droid brains to formulate plans. In this instance, the four thought as one, almost as a hive mind. IG-88A's sentience package, an experimental new technology, allowed him to feel emotions to a limited degree and think in ways normal droids could not. All of these abilities went into making IG-88A an elite killing machine.<ref name="Tale" />

==Equipment==
IG-88A, like all his brethren, had many useful abilities, as he was constructed to be the perfect assassin droid model. He was armed with built-in blasters,<ref name="Tale" /> carried a [[DAS-430 Neural Inhibitor/Legends|DAS-430 Neural Inhibitor]],<ref name="FOC" /> a [[Sonic stunner/Legends|sonic stunner]], a [[paralysis cord]], throwing [[Flechette/Legends|flechettes]], a [[stun pulser]], a cutting [[Laser/Legends|laser]] built into one of his fingers,<ref name="Tale" /> and a [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrower]].<ref name="Guide" /> IG-88A additionally carried [[Concussion grenade/Legends|concussion grenades]] and poisonous gas canisters, and had a [[Scomp link/Legends|computer input port]], giving him a very advanced [[Slicer/Legends|slicing]] system.<ref name="Tale" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Initial backstory===
An IG-88 droid first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. However, ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', released by [[West End Games]] in [[1989]], revealed that there were four IG-88 droids, and another, IG-72, created by Holowan laboratories. It also stated that the droids killed their creators and then escaped, and one of the droids then proceeded to wreak havoc on the galaxy as a bounty hunter. This information was later included in ''[[Galaxy Guide 10: Bounty Hunters]]''. The ''Galaxy Guides'' first created some backstory, including details about the IG-88 droids' activation and the massacre of the Holowan scientists, information that was later included in the [[1996]] book ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]''. However, ''Tales of the Bounty Hunters'', specifically ''[[Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88]]'', by [[Kevin J. Anderson]], then expanded on this information and created new facts about the droids, such as the plan for galactic domination.

''Tales of the Bounty Hunters'' was the also first source to identify the droids as the four models designated A, B, C, and D. In addition, this book established that the IG-88 droid in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' was in fact IG-88B. It also [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] IG-88A to be in control of the Death Star during the Battle of Endor. As the Death Star was destroyed in this battle, the droid's consciousness was established to have been destroyed. However, the droid's body was not destroyed, and IG-88A would appear in later works, such as ''[[Young Jedi Knights: Diversity Alliance]]'', ''[[Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur]]'', and ''[[Young Jedi Knights: The Emperor's Plague]]'', set in 24 ABY, two decades after the Battle of Endor. In ''The Emperor's Plague'', IG-88A's body is destroyed, finally killing him once and for all.

===Character confusion===
An unidentified IG-88 model appears in the [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel]] [[Star Wars comic books|comics]] [[Star Wars (1977) 50|''Star Wars'' (1977) 50]], [[Star Wars (1977) 71|''Star Wars'' (1977) 71]], [[Star Wars (1977) 72|''Star Wars'' (1977) 72]], and [[Star Wars (1977) 85|''Star Wars'' (1977) 85]]. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' establishes that IG-88C and IG-88D are the droids featured in ''The Crimson Forever'', ''Return to Stenos'', and ''Fool's Bounty''. As ''The Hero'' takes place after the destruction of the other three IG-88 models, none of which were known to be repaired, this article assumes that the droid in this comic is IG-88A, who was repaired by Tyko Thul sometime after the Battle of Endor.

An unnamed IG-88 model is also in [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption|''Empire at War: Forces of Corruption'']], set between 3 and 4 ABY. As this model has the ability to hack into the Death Star and take control of its superlaser, this article likewise assumes that this droid is IG-88A. An unidentified IG-88 model appears in ''[[The Bounty Hunters: Kenix Kil]]'' as well. As this story is set in 11 ABY, this article again presumes that this droid is IG-88A.

Though Tyko Thul states that he found and reactivated IG-88A, a date for this is never given, save that it is between 4 and 24 ABY. However, ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'' says that IG-88A was found and reprogrammed by an individual and also appeared on Keyorin. Though this individual is not identified, it is made clear that Thul did not find the droid first, and that IG-88A was in Barpotomous Drebble's possession by a few months after the Battle of Endor. The book also says that the assassin droid was later found on Mechis III by Tyko Thul, who reprogrammed the droid to serve as his guard. This article makes the assumption that IG-88A was first discovered by someone who later gave the droid to Drebble, or Drebble himself, who reprogrammed the droid to act as one of his bodyguards in 4 ABY. The article also assumes, per ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'', that the droid was then left on Mechis III, where he was found by Tyko Thul by 24 ABY, and again reprogrammed.

The droid is also seen roaming the galaxy hunting Kenix Kil in ''The Bounty Hunters: Kenix Kil'', set in 11 ABY. However, this is between the time period when he is shown to be in first Drebble's possession and then Thul's two decades later, so there is no contradiction.
